rules.sentence: Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not construct types implementing `IPartnerClient`.
rules.because: Partner clients are wired with their pooled HttpClient and options in the composition root; constructing one elsewhere bypasses that wiring and the registered lifetime.
rules.fix: Inject IPartnerClient (or IEnumerable<IPartnerClient>); the composition root owns wiring.

rules.sentence: Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not construct `HttpClient`.
rules.because: A new HttpClient per call exhausts sockets under load; IHttpClientFactory pools handlers.
rules.fix: Take a typed or named client from IHttpClientFactory; the exemplar receives its HttpClient through its constructor.

rules.sentence: Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not use `IServiceProvider.GetService()`, `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetService()` or `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetRequiredService()`.
rules.because: Resolving services from IServiceProvider at call sites hides a type's real dependencies; declare them as constructor parameters.
rules.fix: Take the dependency in the constructor; the composition root and its scope seam are the only sanctioned resolve sites.

rules.because: Calling BuildServiceProvider while configuring services builds a second container with its own singletons, a duplicate-instance trap.
rules.fix: Register the dependency and let the host build the provider once; inject what you need.

rules.because: Blocking on a Task or ValueTask (.Result/.Wait/.GetResult) ties up a thread and can deadlock in a captured context; await instead.
rules.fix: Await the call and make the method async; the legacy corner is grandfathered until the SDK exposes async.

migrate.from: A legacy manifest gateway exposes only synchronous calls, so the adapter blocks on async work.

rules.sentence: Types derived from `BackgroundService` must not reference `IOptionsSnapshot<TOptions>` or `IOutboxStore`.
rules.because: A BackgroundService is a singleton; a captured scoped IOptionsSnapshot or scoped store outlives its scope; resolve per work item from an IServiceScopeFactory scope.
rules.fix: Inject IServiceScopeFactory, create a scope per iteration, resolve scoped services inside it.

rules.sentence: Singleton-registered types must not inject scoped-registered types or transient-registered types.
rules.because: A singleton is created once and holds every dependency it injects for the whole process, so a scoped or transient service injected into it is captured past its lifetime and shared across all callers.
rules.fix: Resolve the scoped or transient service per unit of work inside an IServiceScopeFactory scope; take only singleton-safe dependencies in the constructor.

rules.sentence: Methods of authored types in `Meridian.Interchange.*` returning `Task`, `Task<TResult>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` must be named `*Async`.
rules.because: Task- and ValueTask-returning methods carry the Async suffix so callers see at the call site that a method must be awaited.
rules.fix: Rename the method to end in Async.

rules.sentence: Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except types derived from `BackgroundService`, must not swallow `Exception`.
rules.because: Catching base Exception outside a top-level handler swallows the faults you meant to see; scope the catch-all to that handler and let other code catch only the specific types it can handle.
rules.fix: Catch the specific exception you can handle; the only sanctioned catch-all is the dispatcher's poll loop, where OutboxDispatcher logs and continues to the next poll.

rules.sentence: Methods of authored types in `Meridian.Interchange.*` returning `Task`, `Task<TResult>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` must accept a parameter of type `CancellationToken`.
rules.because: Accepting a CancellationToken lets a caller stop in-flight async work and flow that request on to the calls it makes, so a Task- or ValueTask-returning method without one cannot take part in cooperative cancellation.
rules.fix: Add a CancellationToken parameter and flow OutboxDispatcher's stoppingToken through the call chain.

rules.sentence: Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*` must not be attributed with `[Table]` or `[ComplexType]`.
rules.because: A persistence-specific attribute such as [Table] or [ComplexType] couples a persisted type to one data-access technology, so the same model can no longer be stored another way or moved to a new store; keep it ignorant of how it is persisted.
rules.fix: Keep the persisted type a POCO and map it from the persistence layer with fluent configuration (EF Core's IEntityTypeConfiguration, a Dapper column list) instead of attributes on the type.

rules.sentence: Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Outbox.*`, must not expose `OutboxMessage`.
rules.because: Exposing a persisted entity on a public signature couples partner-facing code to the storage model, so a change to how a message is persisted reshapes the partner contract; hand partners a DTO made for the wire instead.
rules.fix: Map the message to a PartnerEnvelope at the OutboxProcessor boundary and expose that; keep OutboxMessage inside the Outbox module.
